No Result View All Result Home News Politics Business Sport Football Health Entertainment Education Opinion Editorial Columns Others LeVogue Magazine Conferences National Economy Contact Us Hausa Edition Home News Politics Business Sport Football Health Entertainment Education Opinion Editorial Columns Others LeVogue Magazine Conferences National Economy Contact Us No Result View All Result No Result View All Result ATAPOLY ASUP Declares Two-Week Warning Strike Over Bauchi Govt’s Failure To Implement CATA, EAA by Khalid Idris Doya 3 seconds ago in Education Share on WhatsApp Share on Facebook Share on X Telegram The Academic Staff Union of Polytechnics (ASUP), Abubakar Tatari Ali Polytechnic (ATAPOLY) Chapter, Bauchi, has declared a two-week warning strike over the failure of the Bauchi State government to implement provisions of the 2026 Federal Government/ASUP Agreement on Consolidated Academic Tools Allowance (CATA) and Earned Academic Allowance (EAA).
The union announced the commencement of the industrial action on Monday in a statement signed by its Chairman, Comrade Nazif Abba Pali, and Secretary, Musa Ibrahim.
According to the statement, the strike took effect on Monday, November 16, 2026, in compliance with a directive of the union’s National Executive Council (NEC).
ASUP said the action followed the state government’s prolonged failure to implement the two allowances despite repeated appeals and engagements, as well as the expiration of a 15-day ultimatum issued by the national leadership of the union.
“The industrial action follows the prolonged failure of the Bauchi State Government to implement the Consolidated Academic Tools Allowance (CATA) and Earned Academic Allowance (EAA) provisions of the 2026 FGN/ASUP Agreement, despite repeated appeals, engagements and the expiration of the 15-day ultimatum issued by the National Body.”
The union consequently directed all academic staff of the institution to suspend academic activities throughout the warning strike.
It listed the affected activities to include lectures, examinations, academic supervision and other academic engagements.
The statement urged members to demonstrate unity, solidarity and discipline during the industrial action, warning against engaging in any academic activity capable of undermining the union’s collective demands.
“The success of this action depends largely on the collective commitment and cooperation of all members,” the statement said.
The union further called on its members to remain steadfast and united until the issues prompting the strike were satisfactorily addressed.
It added that members would be informed of further developments through appropriate organs of the union.
